item.problem_title: Phenotypes enter emulations as error-free binary variables
item.problem_statement: Prescriptions differ from dispensings and dispensings differ from ingestion; diagnostic codes differ from clinical events; death and care outside the system may be incompletely captured. An erroneous weight factor persists in the cumulative weights of every clone that remains at risk. Artificial-censoring membership changes as well, but only where the mismeasured variable enters the strategy, the eligibility rule or the censoring rule. item.paper: Correcting for Measurement Error in Time-Varying Covariates in Marginal Structural Models.
item.evidence: A concrete correction is supplied and its payoff quantified: at high error with strong confounding, two-interval coverage was 0% for the uncorrected weighted model against 78% for indirect correction, and median bias fell by up to 99% at moderate error. Indirect correction is implementable in existing packages, unlike direct correction. What is left open is the class of variables covered: the machinery is for a continuous covariate with a known error variance, entered through the weight model, and says nothing about a binary phenotype defined by codes, where the error is misclassification and no variance parameter exists.

item.problem_title: No estimator is defensible as a default, and no study is required to show that its choice mattered
item.problem_statement: The available estimators differ in what they assume rather than only in how they perform. Active-comparator new-user designs with regression or propensity adjustment handle baseline initiation and not treatment-confounder feedback. Matching gives a transparent population, discards information, and often leaves its estimand unstated. Marginal structural models represent regime effects directly and are unstable under extreme weights. The parametric g-formula supports flexible estimands and is sensitive to sequential outcome-model misspecification. G-estimation avoids modeling the treatment-free outcome distribution and is technically demanding. Longitudinal targeted learning is doubly robust, computationally heavy and sensitive to practical positivity. No estimator is defensible as a universal default, and a study reporting one reports a number whose dependence on that choice is unknown: n
item.paper: An Empirical Method of Detecting Time-Dependent Confounding: An Observational Study of Next Day Delirium in a Medical ICU.
item.evidence: An explicit, prespecifiable criterion is offered for a decision that is normally made by assertion: whether to fit the weighted model at all, based on an ordinal score computed from the exposure and covariate trajectories before the outcome models are compared. Applied to three treatment pairs it produced low, moderate and high, and the estimates moved only for the pair scored high. What it does not close is calibration. The score's validity is judged by whether the weighted and unweighted coefficients differ, which is the comparison the score was meant to spare the analyst, and no threshold is anchored to a known bias.

item.problem_title: There is no assumption dashboard, so diagnosable and undiagnosable assumptions are reported alike
item.problem_statement: Exchangeability and consistency cannot be established from observed data. Neither, strictly, can positivity, model correctness or phenotype validity: the available checks reveal or falsify particular problems and certify none of them. Current reports blur both distinctions. A propensity-score overlap plot is offered and the reader infers that the assumptions have been checked, when the plot is a partial diagnostic of one of them and silent on the rest. No standard panel exists, so what appears varies by author and by journal, and an absent diagnostic cannot be distinguished from one that was run and not reported. A single panel cannot be adequate for every design, which is a constraint on the solution rather than an argument against it.

item.problem_title: Calling an analysis a target trial emulation is treated as evidence about its assumption burden
item.problem_statement: Target trial specification improves temporal alignment, protocol clarity and estimand definition. It does not establish consistency, conditional exchangeability, positivity, valid measurement, correct estimation or transportability, and those are separate conditions rather than steps on one scale: any of them can hold while the others fail. In practice the label does the work of all of them. An analysis that adopts the framework is read as though the whole set had been secured, and no convention asks a study to state the six requirements separately for the estimand it chose. The reporting evidence shows how weakly the label constrains the practice: of 200 published studies claiming to emulate a trial, 43% did not describe all key emulation components.
item.paper: An Empirical Method of Detecting Time-Dependent Confounding: An Observational Study of Next Day Delirium in a Medical ICU.
item.evidence: Fitting the weighted model is explicitly refused as grounds for calling the result unbiased or causal, on the stated ground that capturing all covariates and having no unmeasured factors are very strong assumptions. That is the correct separation between the method label and the assumption burden, made in the same document that fits the method. It closes nothing structurally: the refusal is a sentence in a discussion, not a reporting requirement, and the same analysis presented with the causal vocabulary would be indistinguishable in its numbers.

item.problem_title: The visit process is treated as a nuisance to be imputed rather than as part of the causal structure
item.problem_statement: Biomarkers and diagnoses are observed when a patient attends care and a clinician orders a test. That visit process depends on latent severity, on prior treatment and often on an impending outcome, so missing-at-random conditional on the recorded history can fail precisely because the recording is itself informative, last observation carried forward constructs a history in which the absence of measurement was itself evidence, and conditioning on having been observed can induce selection bias. Three estimator families now address this: multiply robust estimation under covariate-driven observation times, calibrated inverse probability weights under irregular visits, and continuous-time weights built from a marked point process. item.problem_title: Identification of dynamic regimes in continuous time under treatment-dependent observation is unresolved
item.problem_statement: Treatments, outcomes and clinical observations occur asynchronously and are recorded at times determined by the care process. Discretizing that onto a grid can reverse the temporal ordering of a treatment and an outcome falling in the same interval, merge several events into one, and define an estimand that exists only relative to the chosen interval. Identification and efficient estimation for dynamic interventions in continuous time under counting-process filtrations and irregular monitoring have been established. They do not yet settle the case an emulation on routine data actually faces: a visit process that depends on treatment, combined with effects that occur inside an interval. item.paper: The Impact of Different CD4 Cell-Count Monitoring and Switching Strategies on Mortality in HIV-Infected African Adults on Antiretroviral Therapy: An Application of Dynamic Marginal Structural Models.
item.evidence: A concrete identification route is supplied for regimes indexed by the observation process, resting on the assumption that performing the CD4 test has no effect on survival except through its result. It operates on a discrete 4-week interval grid with a fixed monitoring frequency per strategy. Continuous-time switching and observation schedules that respond to patient state are outside what the construction covers.

item.problem_title: Variance estimation after cloning and sequence expansion has no scalable, correct default
item.problem_statement: Sequential emulation and cloning expand a dataset by orders of magnitude: a row per eligible decision point per person, multiplied by the strategies each person is initially compatible with. Two dependence structures result, repeated participation and clone-level copies of one history, and naive standard errors ignore both. Person-clustered sandwich inference handles both scalably when the weights are treated as fixed or the estimating-equation conditions hold, and for parametric marginal structural models with inverse probability weighting there are now evaluated alternatives with simulation guidance on coverage against cost. No default handles the harder case: clone-level dependence together with site clustering and the uncertainty from weights estimated by flexible nuisance models, at sequence-expansion scale. The bootstrap that would is correct in principle and prohibitive in practic
item.paper: Identifying a set that contains the best dynamic treatment regimes.
item.evidence: Each participant contributes to every embedded regime compatible with the observed treatment path, so the regime-specific estimators are correlated by construction and the correlation is not known in advance. A derivation of that correlation structure is supplied and used to build the simultaneous inference. What is not closed is the general case: the derivation leans on known randomization probabilities at both stages, which an observational sequential emulation does not have.

item.evidence: The estimator choice is shown to change the reported conclusion, not merely its precision: the augmented estimator cut standard errors by up to 60% at n between 100 and 400 and produced a strictly smaller set of candidate best regimes at every sample size while holding the Type I error rate.
